From August 17 to 21, 2017, GEYK members Kim Se-jin, Kim Jin-young, and Cho Hye-won traveled to Taiwan for the third East Asia Climate Leadership Camp (EACLC).

The camp brings together 350.org partner activists from East and Southeast Asia to train, share what they know, learn together, and work toward common climate goals. Forty young people came from South Korea, China, Japan, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, and elsewhere in the region.

On the first day, we shared food and got to know one another at orientation. On the second, we learned about the Taichung Power Plant and visited it. We also met nearby residents and heard painful accounts: mothers and children developing asthma, families losing someone to cancer, and a person who had monitored workers’ health and joined a campaign after seeing how the plant affected it. At the power plant, we saw foul-smelling, foamy water being discharged into the sea even though it had reportedly been treated. We were all shocked.

On the third day, we reviewed NGO activities in each country, wrote down our goals, and shared them. On the fourth, we imagined the future we wanted and took part in an exercise about the power of investors whose decisions harm the environment. We shared our cultures with one another and enjoyed learning about Taiwan’s Hakka culture on the final day.

The schedule was demanding, but we were grateful for everything we learned and experienced. We believe everyone who joined will continue working for climate action across Asia. Thank you, 350.org!
